## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet. The starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds, so I can't rank anything by dev success. For now the priority is to get any learning at all, not to refine the architecture. The cheapest lever is the sample budget. With the default 4 PPO epochs the run gets about 131k steps. Two epochs give about 243k and one epoch gives about 426k, with r staying near 1. This round compares 1 and 2 epochs on the unchanged starting network, and tests a new network whose compute is about the same as the starting one (r about 1). That network has learned per-footprint convolutions and a dilated trunk with a larger receptive field, and it uses 1 epoch so it can be compared directly with candidate A. If dev success stays at 0 everywhere, the next round should compare training success and returns to see which runs are learning.

### Round 2
All four trials so far, including the baseline, score exactly 0 on dev. Training success is also 0 at 1, 2 and 4 epochs, and with a learned footprint head. Using fewer epochs to collect about 3x more samples did not start learning, so sample count alone is not the blocker. Training takes only about 70 s of the 900 s limit, so there is a lot of time headroom. Training success of 0 over about 400k steps is suspicious and may mean the world differs from its description. Two possible causes are a different action or anchor indexing, which a strictly aligned per-cell convolutional head cannot fix, and credit for the end bonus that a short horizon cannot reach. This round tests three things separately: (1) the recipe, with longer-horizon credit (gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95); (2) an extra flattened linear placement head that does not assume cell alignment; (3) a small transformer whose learned positional embeddings and global attention can learn any cell-to-action mapping and give global context for DONE.

### Round 3
All 6 trials scored 0 on dev and also 0 on training success. That covers 1, 2 and 4 PPO epochs, gamma 0.99, a flat head and a transformer. So neither sample count, credit assignment, action misalignment nor the trunk type has unblocked learning. Training uses under 80 s of the 900 s limit, so compute is the only budget that binds. At 1 epoch and r ≤ 1 we already get the most samples possible, about 405k steps. I suspect early collapse onto DONE. Random placements mostly fill cells outside the target, which gives negative reward, so ending the episode at once (reward 0) wins early on and exploration dies. Since priors about samples, gamma and the head were not supported, this round tests the optimisation dynamics: entropy with more gradient steps, slower and safer updates, and a DONE path with legality input that starts out neutral.

### Round 4
Nine trials have run, and every one scored 0 on dev success and 0 on training success. The changes tested so far: PPO epochs 1, 2 and 4 (the samples prior did not help); gamma 0.99 with lambda 0.95; entropy coefficient 0.03 with more minibatches; a lower lr with a tighter clip; a learned footprint head with a dilated trunk; a small flat head that can map any cell to any action; a cell transformer; and the mask as an input with a DONE head driven by per-cell features. None of these priors is supported yet, but zero against zero says nothing about their effect sizes. Possible blockers that remain untested: the actions may map to cells in a way that local heads cannot learn (the flat head had little capacity); each sample may give too little learning to a small network; and the policy may stay too flat for the greedy choice to be exact. This is the last round and any non-zero score beats the baseline, so I am spreading the three candidates across these three hypotheses.
